# The shape that was mistaken for a gate bug (see scripts/ci-gates-test.sh).
#
# A PR made things slightly slower: sec/op rises a few percent (well under the
# timing gate), B/op and allocs/op are flat, and the B/s throughput column --
# where NEGATIVE means slower -- dips by several percent.
#
# The magnitudes in the B/s column (up to -5.97%) are the only ones in the run
# above BENCH_ALLOC_THRESHOLD_PCT, which makes it tempting to conclude that B/s
# is being judged against the allocation gate. It is not: is_alloc_metric()
# requires a "/op" suffix, so B/s falls through to the timing gate, and the
# report prints "(gate 15%) (higher is better)" on each of these rows.
#
# This fixture pins that. The gate must exit 0 here.
#
# Rows are verbatim from the live run on luthersystems/elps PR #310
# (actions/runs/31222414614), minus the one row that legitimately fired --
# a +8.44% B/op allocation regression, kept separately in
# benchstat-alloc-regression-live.txt.
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/luthersystems/elps/parser/rdparser
cpu: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
